absolute-advantage.def: The ability to produce more of a good than another producer with the same resources, or the same amount with fewer resources.

comparative-advantage.def: The ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another producer. Specializing by comparative advantage is what creates gains from trade.

specialization.def: Concentrating production on the goods a person or country makes at the lowest opportunity cost, and trading for the rest.

terms-of-trade.def: The rate at which one good is exchanged for another in trade, such as 1 hat for 2.5 shirts. Both sides gain when it lies between their two opportunity costs.

gains-from-trade.def: The extra goods both sides get when they specialize by comparative advantage and trade, letting each consume beyond its own production possibilities.

output-input-method.def: Two ways to read trade data. Output data give units made per worker (the cost of one good is the other good's output divided by its own); input data give hours per unit (the cost of one good is its own hours divided by the other good's hours).
